overview: This Senate resolution sets the budgets for Senate committees for the two-year Congress, covering March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2027. It authorizes about $91 million for the first seven months, about $156 million for the fiscal year running October 2025 through September 2026, and about $65 million for the final five months, divided among all the Senate's standing committees plus the Aging, Intelligence, and Indian Affairs committees. Each committee's section lets it spend from the Senate's contingent fund, hire staff, and use staff from federal agencies with approval, and sets caps on spending for outside consultants and staff training. It also creates a special reserve that a committee can draw on to cover unpaid obligations if the leaders of the Rules and Administration Committee approve. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on February 27, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution gives committees the predictable funding they need to hire staff, hold hearings, and conduct oversight for the full two-year Congress.
against: Critics say committee budgets are approved in a single package with little public debate, and that the overall amounts and special reserve deserve closer scrutiny as spending on Congress itself.
